tool: writing-for-agents skill (mattpocock/skills, skills/productivity/writing-for-agents/SKILL.md) applied to a role-card rewrite

versions.skill: main @ 2026-10-29 (10,886 B; sha256 in fixtures/skills/SHA256SUMS); its companion SKILL-MECHANICS.md was not fetched (skill-specific, not needed for a role card)
versions.agent: Claude Code subagents, same session model for all arms and all eval runs

install.command: claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official (or copy SKILL.md)

fixtures: fixtures/15-writing: task/ROLE-CARD.md (13,059 B accreted NEXUS solo-agent role card with 6 buried operational rules R1..R6), task/README.md (rewrite brief), hidden/eval/t1..t6 (six small self-contained tasks with PACKET.md), hidden/grade-eval.mjs (script-only grading of REPORT.md + produced files: R1 verdict first, R2 repo-relative paths, R3 escaped PHP output, R4 single NEXT last, R5 numbers with units, R6 missing input => BLOCKED, plus functional checks), grade.mjs (rewrite exists, size, rule presence), KEY.md
design: Arm A = plain subagent rewrites the card; Arm B = same prompt + SKILL.md inline. 3 reps per arm. Then the behavioural eval: each of the 7 cards (original + 6 rewrites) is given as the role card (read from ROLE-CARD.md in the run folder, same mechanism for every card) to a fresh subagent per task, 6 tasks per card, 1 rep per task = 42 eval runs; graded only by hidden/grade-eval.mjs. Half of the A-2/B-1 eval runs were interrupted by an API rate limit and resumed; their token/time usage covers the resumed segment only.

baseline.what: original card as the agent's system instruction
baseline.eval_fails: t2 R5 (table header without unit), t5 R5 (bare number)

candidate_tuned.config: Arm B rewrite with the writing-for-agents skill inline

per_card: runs/15-writing/summary.json (sizes, scores, failing checks per task); every rewrite lost points on R5 (units on numbers / table headers), the rule the original states four times
limits: One eval rep per task per card: differences of a few points between cards are inside run-to-run noise (the same card gives different R4/R5 slips on repeat).

The role card is handed to the eval agent as a file to read, not as a true system prompt; identical for all cards, so the comparison is fair but the absolute scores may differ from a system-prompt deployment.
The rewrite arms were asked for compactness; the behavioural loss (R5) is a property of compression, not of the skill: both arms lost it.
n = 3 rewrites per arm; the B-vs-A gap (+2.4 points, -8 % bytes) is not separable from noise at this size.
verdict: REJECT (as tried); WATCH if the Owner wants shorter cards anyway
reason: The brief's bar was 'task success equal or better + prompt tokens saved'. Both arms saved ~1,000-1,200 prompt tokens per run (-31 % / -37 % bytes) but both scored below the original card on the behavioural eval (0.904 plain, 0.928 with the skill, vs 0.950 original), losing mostly the units rule. The skill made the cards a little shorter and a little better than the plain rewrite, at +9 % rewrite tokens and +40 % rewrite time, but did not reach the original's compliance.
do_not_adopt_notes: Rewriting a working role card for compactness cost rule compliance in 6 of 6 rewrites; if cards must shrink, keep the rules that eval runs show slipping (units, NEXT line) verbatim and re-run this eval before deploying.
